Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator (QEMU functional + vsim cycle-accurate, two-phase handoff QEMU1 -> vsim).
CANONICAL docs that are the source of truth and MUST be kept (do not recommend deleting these): CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md (always-current user guide), docs/FRS.md, docs/MRD.md, ROADMAP.md (master FR tracker, "single source of truth"), driver/ROADMAP.md (C++ andes-sim driver tracker), docs/engine_interface.md, docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb (the L-id capability-gap envelope).
The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `andes_sim_runtime_lib.md`

Steps:
1. Read `andes_sim_runtime_lib.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`

  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
(`./andes-sim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.

Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andes-sim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).
